title: finite
body:
Terminating in a bounded number of steps, rather than possibly running forever.

The word appears in this course because of [[Progress]]: the procedure that decides which
waiting thread enters the [[Critical Section]] next must itself be finite. If deciding who
goes in could take unboundedly long, nobody gets in, and the decision procedure has become
the thing it was meant to arbitrate. A decision rule that scanned an ever-growing list, or
one that could loop while two threads keep changing their flags, is not finite in this
sense.

Finiteness of the decision is what makes [[Bounded Waiting]] achievable: you cannot put an
upper bound on time in the entry section if the step that admits you has no bound of its own.
